check_connection.title: Check the connection
check_connection.description: Call the merchant endpoint the connector's own catalogue entry declares, with a limit of one, to confirm the credentials and keys work. This is the only DataCandy endpoint this package can vouch for, and it is what the connector verifies with.

limit.description: How many records to ask for. One is enough to prove the credential works.

output.description: The first merchant record, which is enough to confirm the credentials and keys are accepted.

list_merchants.title: List merchants
list_merchants.description: List the merchants visible to these credentials. The same endpoint the connector verifies with, used for its actual purpose. `limit` and `offset` are DataCandy's usual paging parameters; pass any further filters the account's own documentation names through the raw GET tool instead of guessing them here.

offset.description: How many records to skip, for paging.

output.description: The merchants this access key can see.

call_datacandy_api_get.title: Read from the API (GET)
call_datacandy_api_get.description: GET any path on DataCandy's API with this connection's credentials applied, for the parts of the surface the named tools above do not cover. You must know the provider's API; nothing here validates the path. Prefer a named tool wherever one exists.

path.description: Path to call, relative to the connection's base url.

query.description: Query-string parameters as a flat object, e.g. {"limit": 50}.

output.description: Whatever DataCandy's API returns for that request, parsed as JSON where possible.

call_datacandy_api_post.title: Send data to the API (POST)
call_datacandy_api_post.description: POST to any path on DataCandy's API with this connection's credentials applied. A general-purpose escape hatch for the parts of the surface the named tools above do not cover; it makes no claim about which endpoints exist, and a POST can create real records.

path.description: Path to call, relative to the connection's base url.

query.description: Query-string parameters as a flat object.

output.description: Whatever DataCandy's API returns for that request, parsed as JSON where possible.

call_datacandy_api_put.title: Replace a resource at the API (PUT)
call_datacandy_api_put.description: PUT to any path on DataCandy's API with this connection's credentials applied, for the parts of the surface the named tools above do not cover. A PUT replaces rather than merges, so an omitted field is usually cleared.

path.description: Path to call, relative to the connection's base url.

query.description: Query-string parameters as a flat object.

output.description: Whatever DataCandy's API returns for that request, parsed as JSON where possible.

call_datacandy_api_patch.title: Partially update a resource at the API (PATCH)
call_datacandy_api_patch.description: PATCH any path on DataCandy's API with this connection's credentials applied, for the parts of the surface the named tools above do not cover. You must know the provider's API; nothing here validates the path.

path.description: Path to call, relative to the connection's base url.

query.description: Query-string parameters as a flat object.

output.description: Whatever DataCandy's API returns for that request, parsed as JSON where possible.

call_datacandy_api_delete.title: Delete a resource at the API (DELETE)
call_datacandy_api_delete.description: DELETE any path on DataCandy's API with this connection's credentials applied, for the parts of the surface the named tools above do not cover. Irreversible, and nothing here checks what the path points at.

path.description: Path to call, relative to the connection's base url.

query.description: Query-string parameters as a flat object.

output.description: Whatever DataCandy's API returns for that request, parsed as JSON where possible.
